blocks.title: Conjugated diene
blocks.text: A diene is a molecule containing two carbon-carbon double bonds. In a conjugated diene the double bonds in the carbon chain are separated by a single bond.

The adjacent double bonds of a conjugated diene allow the overlap of p orbitals on three or more adjacent atoms. This overlap leads to a delocalisation of electrons, which can stabilise the molecule and affect its reactivity; in conjugated dienes the pi overlap extends over the entire system. Conjugated alkenes have unique properties because of the arrangement of their double bonds; conjugated dienes such as buta-1,3-diene are used to produce synthetic rubber, the conjugated structure allowing polymerisation into long chains with rubber-like properties.
Draw buta-1,3-diene, illustrate the delocalisation of its electrons, and explain why conjugated alkenes may react differently from isolated ones.
